newsitem.title: UK: Brazil, Russia, Bulgaria Bradys under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Russia, Bulgaria Bradys under pressure.

text.p: Brady bonds generally held up as the drop in U.S. Treasuries came to a halt on Monday, but political concerns hurt Bulgaria and took some of the lustre off Brazil.
Russia also slid though there appeared to be no fresh news driving prices down.
Bulgaria continues to get hit as political unrest grows in the country and the threat that already lethargic economic reform will be even further delayed.
Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were quoted more than a point lower at 48-1/2 cents in the dollar.

Protests against the ruling Socialists, spurred by soaring inflation, are growing and the country's trade unions are now threatening one-hour warning strikes to press demands for an early general election.
Traders said they wanted to see Brady payments made, as promised, at the end of this month and a deal with the International Monetary Fund, which requires the setting up of a currency board.
An IMF official told Reuters in Sofia that the Fund was prepared to complete talks on a new loan as soon as a stable government was in place.

Late last week, outgoing President Zhelyu Zhelev postponed handing a mandate to the man nominated by the ruling Socialists as prime miniser, Nikolai Dobrev, until the party agrees to hold an election two years ahead of schedule.
Brazilian Bradys were off about half a point, after the country's biggest party voted to delay a bill that would allow President Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term.
Traders said the market sees any threats to Cardoso's future as a threat to economic reforms under his rule.
Brazil C bonds fell half a point to a bid of 74 percent of face value.
Russian debt has come under some pressure from President Boris Yeltsin's ill health, but one trader said Monday's weakness appeared to be due to one large local seller rather than any fresh news.
The latest reports from Moscow said Yeltsin was stable and recovering in the hospital from pneumonia.

Traders said the rest of the market held up well in the face of last Friday's weaker U.S. Treasuries, which now appear to have settled after being unnerved by the December payroll figures. -- Jonathan Thatcher, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7770 (fax +44 171 583 7239)
